newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called lower tracking ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called lower tracking ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called lower Thursday tracking ACCESS on no news after a late session sell-off Wednesday left oil prices technically weakened, dealers said.
"We are just seeing technical follow-through from yesterday when both crude and gasoline hit trendline resistance and went lower," said Victor Yu, vice president of Refco Inc in New York.
Crude was called 10 to 15 cents a barrel lower. Refined products were called steady to 0.25 cent a gallon lower.

On Wednesday, May heating oil ended 0.84 cent a gallon lower at 58.07 cents. June crude ended 23 cents a barrel lower at $20.21. May gasoline bucked trends, settling 0.55 cent up at 63.91 cents a gallon, though still off its session high of 64.50 cents.

The expiry in the May refined product contract has left a rollover gap in spot heating oil from 54.92 to 58.07. Some dealers note the short covering which has fueled recent strength in spot month product prices has partly dried up, though others think the spot rollover gaps will be filled.

"I think the gap will be filled since we have seen some good implied demand in heat and stocks are still relatively tight," said Bob MacMinn, president of MPAS Inc in Toronto, of the heating oil gap in June.

But, MacMinn said ample crude supply will leave prompt month crude vulnerable as shorts are squeezed from the market. On Wednesday, June crude rose to $20.53 where it failed at trendline resistance on the spot chart that stems from the session high on January 31 of $24.87.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
